mechanism_narrative: Low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which stimulates economic growth and increases S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when FEDFUNDS is low, contradicting the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment rate signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer confidence and S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when UNRATE drops below 5%, refuting the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Combined strength in employment and low unemployment indicates a robust economy, positively influencing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not positively correlated with joint labor market strength.

mechanism_narrative: GDP growth above a certain threshold indicates strong economic demand, leading to higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative despite GDP growth exceeding 2.5%, disproving the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation leads to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are positive when CPIAUCSL exceeds 220, contradicting the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Strong housing market, indicated by high housing starts, signals economic strength and boosts S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative when HOUST exceeds 1000, refuting the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth indicates a strong supply chain, supporting higher S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are not positively correlated with INDPRO growth.

mechanism_narrative: Strong GDP growth combined with controlled inflation indicates a balanced economy, positively influencing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 returns are negative despite GDPC1 and CPIAUCSL conditions, disproving the hypothesis.
